+title: Port DeepseekV4 Compressor/Indexer sparse attention (long-context path)
+---
+## What
+
+Create `Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/DeepseekV4Compressor.swift` — DSV4's compressed sparse attention (`Compressor` + `Indexer`), the mechanism behind its 1M-token context.
+
+**Deliberately deferred until basic support works.** Everything before this task ships a working DSV4 for short prompts; `sanitize` in task `pwr8r3h` drops `compressor.*` and `indexer.*` keys precisely so the model loads without this. That filter must be **removed** as part of this task.
+
+Port from `scouzi1966/mlx-swift-lm` @ `main`, `Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/DeepseekV4Compressor.swift` (1164 lines).
+
+Config drivers (already decoded by task `6f6qmf7`): `sliding_window=128`, `compress_ratios[i] ∈ {4, 128, 0}` selecting per-layer behavior, `index_n_heads`, `index_head_dim`, `index_topk`. Layers with `compress_ratio == 0` use plain attention; nonzero values engage the compressor at that ratio.
+
+This is the same architectural family as the sparse attention upstream `mlx-lm` introduced in `mlx_lm/models/deepseek_v32.py` — worth reading as a second reference, since we do **not** have a `deepseek_v32` port to build on.
+
+Sizing warning: at 1164 reference lines this is the largest single unit in the workstream and likely exceeds the 500-line guideline. If it cannot land as one coherent, testable unit, split it — a reasonable seam is `Indexer` (top-k selection) first, then `Compressor` (pooled KV), since the indexer's causal top-k is independently testable. `osaurus-ai/vmlx-swift-lm` has a dedicated `Tests/MLXLMTests/DeepseekV4IndexerCausalTopKTests.swift`, which suggests that seam is real.
+
+## Provenance
+- Reference: `scouzi1966/mlx-swift-lm` @ `main` — `Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/DeepseekV4Compressor.swift` (MIT; header attributes Osaurus AI).
+- Test-shape hint: `osaurus-ai/vmlx-swift-lm` — `Tests/MLXLMTests/DeepseekV4IndexerCausalTopKTests.swift`, `Tests/MLXLMTests/DeepseekV4CacheDiskRoundTripTests.swift`.
+- Second reference for the sparse-attention family: `ml-explore/mlx-lm` `mlx_lm/models/deepseek_v32.py`.
+- Apply the attribution header decided in task `jhk0apk`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/DeepseekV4Compressor.swift` exists with the `Compressor` and `Indexer` modules.
+- [ ] The `compressor.*` / `indexer.*` drop filter is removed from `DeepseekV4Model.sanitize`, and those weights now load.
+- [ ] Indexer top-k selection is strictly causal — no position attends to a future position.
+- [ ] Layers with `compress_ratio == 0` still take the plain-attention path, unchanged.
+- [ ] Short-prompt output is unchanged from before this task (no regression to the already-shipped path).
+- [ ] A long-context prompt (beyond `sliding_window=128`) produces coherent output.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] New `Tests/MLXLMTests/DeepseekV4IndexerTests.swift`: causal-mask property test — for every query position, every selected key index is ≤ the query index, across randomized inputs.
+- [ ] New `Tests/MLXLMTests/DeepseekV4CompressorTests.swift`: pooled-KV shape for `compress_ratio` 4 and 128; `allFinite`.
+- [ ] Test: `compress_ratio == 0` path is bit-identical to the plain-attention path.
+- [ ] Test: `sanitize` no longer drops `compressor.*`/`indexer.*` (inverse of the assertion added in task `pwr8r3h`).
+- [ ] Regression: re-run `swift test --filter DeepseekV4ModelTests` — still green, proving short prompts did not change.
+- [ ] Run: `swift test --filter 'DeepseekV4Indexer|DeepseekV4Compressor'` — all pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — start with the indexer causal-mask property test; it is cheap and catches the classic off-by-one.

 assignees:

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01kzpb3n0fqspjaq9ctst5dq5s
+  text: |-
+    ### Layer rule for the indexer -- this card does not state it yet
+
+    From task `^wkv5j6f`, measured on `Tests/MLXLMTests/Resources/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-4bit-config.json`:
+
+    - The published `quantization` block names indexer keys for the **21 even layers 2 to 42** only -- 84 keys: `wq_b`, `weights_proj`, `compressor.wgate` and `compressor.wkv` on each. These are the layers whose compress ratio is 4. The odd layers 3 to 41 hold a ratio of 128 and hold no indexer, and layers 0 and 1 hold a ratio of 0 and hold neither an indexer nor a compressor.
+    - This card names `index_n_heads`, `index_head_dim` and `index_topk` only, and states nothing about which layers hold indexer weights. An indexer built on all 43 layers, or on all 41 compressor layers, fails the weight load.
+    - `Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/DeepseekV4Configuration.swift` holds `hasCompressor(layer:)` and **no** `hasIndexer(layer:)` beside it. Add one -- `compressRatios[layer] == 4`, with the same bound guard -- and build the indexer submodule only where it gives true.
+    - `compress_ratios` holds **44** entries while `num_hidden_layers` is **43**, and entry 43 is 0. The bound guard makes `hasCompressor(layer:)` correct today. Any code that reads `compressRatios.count` as a layer count gets 44. Read `numHiddenLayers` for a layer count.
+
+    `Tests/MLXLMTests/DeepseekV4QuantizationPlanTests.swift` pins the layer rule in `fixtureNamesIndexerKeysOnTheEvenLayersFromTwoUp`.
+  timestamp: 2026-08-10T17:21:44.975894+00:00
